High-access external assessment

An outside estimate of AI speeding up AI research

EVENT / 2026-11-05
REVIEW / 2026-11-06

Capability signal / heavily redacted
What the source reports
After eleven weeks of access to internal data, METR's subjective best guess is that Anthropic is improving its models on well-specified tasks at about twice its March 2024–October 2025 rate, with high uncertainty (1.3x–3x would not surprise METR). It attributes perhaps 80% of the current acceleration to Anthropic's own use of AI and found no clear bottleneck for the next 12 months, while saying it may be missing some.
Our reading
The first outside, quantified estimate we have seen that AI is materially accelerating frontier AI development. It makes the mechanism behind our improvement-loop question more concrete.
What it does not establish
Same research lineage as our other METR entries. The developer redacted the evidence METR found most informative, so readers cannot check it and must rely on the assessor's judgment. The benchmark-trend estimate is 1.9x (95% interval 1.5–2.8x), ranges from 1.1x to 2.9x depending on the link function, and is 1.4x when other labs' models are included. The roughly 12x self-reported staff uplift comes from Slack emoji polls, which METR calls very loose evidence; it is not a measured speed-up. AI did most of the analysis, and our pipeline uses the same model family. The assessed company improves its own frontier models rather than running a preregistered, independently reproduced checkpoint series, so this is not a qualifying record.
Compared with expectations
Supports the mechanism behind improvement-loop without meeting its criteria. No forecast revision is inferred, and the curve stays schematic.

02 / MAKE EXPECTATIONS TESTABLE

SUPERFORECASTING / QUESTION DESIGN

Smaller questions.
Sharper updates.

How far to singularity has no agreed measuring stick. These registered milestone forecasts make parts of the ambition resolvable. Each percentage is our subjective chance of a qualifying new public record by its deadline—not confidence that the curve position is accurate.

Q01 / Scientific workBY 2028-12-31

Can AI originate independently accepted research?

65%
CHANCE OF YESNew public record by 2028-12-31
Issued 5 November 2026 · open forecast

Subjective estimate, not an empirical base rate or a singularity probability.

Why we think this may happen

  • The Station paper reports exact constructions or Lean-verified proofs and release of source, agent dialogues and verification code. That is relevant to provenance and correctness gates, though author reports alone do not establish independent endorsement.
  • The AI Scientist-v2 and Co-Scientist represent distinct organisational research lineages. Their public papers show routes to autonomous idea development and experimental follow-through rather than just answering examinations.
  • The deadline leaves just over two years for new work, reproduction and substantive reuse to become public; formal domains can complete correctness checks faster than long physical experiments.

Why we might be wrong

  • The research may remain concentrated in mathematics/computer science; calling neighbouring subfields two distinct domains would weaken the original question and must not be used to force YES.
  • AI-generated novelty can turn out to reproduce training material or a human-provided mechanism. Better provenance may disqualify apparently strong cases, moving the probability down.
  • Wet-lab verification may be done only by collaborators, while independent reuse and unaffiliated expert endorsements arrive after2028.
  • Conversely, open proof artefacts and independently run verifiers could make the strict validation gates easier than assumed, moving the probability up.
Exact outcome, timeframe & update signals +
What counts as YES
A qualifying public record must first be published from 6 November 2026 through 2028-12-31. Previously published cases inform this forecast but do not count as outcomes. At least two results from unaffiliated teams in two distinct domains. Each publishes provenance showing the decisive mechanism was absent from the human brief, passes blind independent reproduction or formal verification, and receives public correctness-and-novelty endorsement from two unaffiliated experts or substantive independent reuse. All evidence must be publicly available by the deadline.
Resolution source & edge cases
Public papers, released provenance and independent validation records. Ambiguous provenance leaves the case unqualified; no public qualifying record by the deadline resolves NO. Only records first published within the stated prospective observation window count.
Observation window
6 November 2026 through 2028-12-31 at 23:59 UTC. Criteria version 1.0. Previously published cases do not count as new outcomes.
Evidence that would raise the probability
A newly published first-domain case meets every gate, including independently checked provenance and either qualifying unaffiliated endorsements or substantive reuse, while an unaffiliated team has a concrete second-domain result under external validation. Proposed likelihood-ratio multiplier: 2.0. This is an update rule for review, not an automatic score.
Evidence that would lower it
By end2027, the strongest new cases repeatedly fail provenance/novelty review or lack independent reproduction, leaving no fully qualifying first-domain case. Proposed likelihood-ratio multiplier: 0.5. This is an update rule for review, not an automatic score.
How we estimated this +
One contributing analyst’s starting point
Explicit subjective prior of 50%, not a measured base rate: the class is publicly attributable AI-originated scientific results with external validation. Requiring two domains, unaffiliated producers and independent validation makes this materially harder than paper generation or peer-review acceptance. The prior expresses uncertainty about crossing all gates within just over two years, rather than assuming that any existing headline already qualifies.
Reference-class limitations
Claimed autonomous research results with released provenance plus external validation. Nearby anchors include Sakana's workshop review experiment, algorithmic constructions and wet-lab hypothesis work; they have incompatible denominators and weaker or different endpoints. Their rates cannot be pooled.
Combining perspectives
Equal-weight geometric mean of odds from two separately elicited research perspectives, with no extremizing. They share model-family and source dependencies; this is not an independent human ensemble or evidence of calibration.
Limits of confidence
Subjective probability, not an empirical base rate. No matched reference-class frequency was found. Whole-percentage presentation does not imply one-point precision. Analyst spread is disagreement, not a confidence interval.
Separately elicited views
55% / 74%. The spread reflects analyst disagreement, not a confidence interval. Shared model-family and source dependencies limit the ensemble.
Current record
Forecast #1 · initial estimate 65% · not yet resolved or scored.

Q02 / Physical workBY 2028-12-31

Will a newly reported AI-originated physical component clear qualification?

72%
CHANCE OF YESNew public record by 2028-12-31
Issued 5 November 2026 · open forecast

Subjective estimate, not an empirical base rate or a singularity probability.

Why we think this may happen

  • NASA's technical record explicitly reports computer-evolved ST5 antenna designs approved for deployment and flight-qualified; the JPL design page and completed mission record corroborate the historical engineering pathway. The old case informs the prior and cannot resolve the corrected new-publication window.
  • NASA's Evolved Structures paper provides detailed AI-generated mechanical component provenance and physical tests. This establishes an active engineering route, while tests alone do not satisfy the named acceptance gate.
  • Google's primary AlphaChip account describes circuit-block layouts used in production TPU generations, extending the plausible opportunity set beyond mechanical components. Its production-use claim is not itself treated as a qualifying public formal acceptance record.
  • Only one bounded new component is required, and the criterion permits engineering fields with shorter qualification paths than therapeutic approval.

Why we might be wrong

  • The decisive candidate may actually be selected by engineers after AI proposes alternatives. Mere AI assistance must not be relabelled as AI selection.
  • Qualification evidence may remain confidential; production deployment or a press release without the named acceptance authority and intended use should not silently substitute for the required record.
  • Spaceflight research tests can remain demonstrations, and drug clinical progress is not approval for routine therapeutic use. Mixing these endpoints would overstate progress.
  • The historical antenna sits ambiguously between circuit and mechanical categories; the forecast does not rely on counting it as a qualifying new case, but an overly broad reading of categories would inflate the estimate.
Exact outcome, timeframe & update signals +
What counts as YES
A qualifying public record must first be published from 6 November 2026 through 2028-12-31. Previously published cases inform this forecast but do not count as outcomes. At least one bounded molecule, material, circuit block or mechanical component has public provenance showing AI selected the decisive candidate, plus a named regulator's or production-qualification authority's acceptance for its intended use. Both records must be public by the deadline. A patent, simulation or research demonstration alone does not qualify.
Resolution source & edge cases
Public provenance and the named qualification record. No publicly documented case satisfying both gates by the deadline resolves NO. This does not establish that no private case exists. Only records first published within the stated prospective observation window count.
Observation window
6 November 2026 through 2028-12-31 at 23:59 UTC. Criteria version 1.0. Previously published cases do not count as new outcomes.
Evidence that would raise the probability
A post-cutoff candidate has public AI-selection provenance, independently documented physical testing and a named qualification programme scheduled to decide before end2028. Proposed likelihood-ratio multiplier: 2.0. This is an update rule for review, not an automatic score.
Evidence that would lower it
By end2027, candidate reports consistently disclose human decisive selection or decline to release acceptance records; no public candidate with a named pending qualification can be identified. Proposed likelihood-ratio multiplier: 0.5. This is an update rule for review, not an automatic score.
How we estimated this +
One contributing analyst’s starting point
Explicit subjective prior of75%, not an observed candidate-to-qualification rate. Outside-view evidence establishes that algorithm-originated flight hardware and AI-designed production circuit layouts are not unprecedented. Over a little more than two years, one additional publicly documented bounded case across several engineering domains is more plausible than a first-ever breakthrough. A complete public acceptance/provenance package is still uncertain.
Reference-class limitations
Newly public bounded components whose AI design/selection provenance and intended-use qualification are both documented. Domains remain separate: spacecraft components, circuit blocks, materials and molecules have different clocks. No cross-domain average success rate is asserted.
Combining perspectives
Equal-weight geometric mean of odds from two separately elicited research perspectives, with no extremizing. They share model-family and source dependencies; this is not an independent human ensemble or evidence of calibration.
Limits of confidence
Subjective probability, not an empirical base rate. No matched reference-class frequency was found. Whole-percentage presentation does not imply one-point precision. Analyst spread is disagreement, not a confidence interval.
Separately elicited views
78% / 64%. The spread reflects analyst disagreement, not a confidence interval. Shared model-family and source dependencies limit the ensemble.

Q03 / Cumulative improvementBY 2029-12-31

Can improvement persist across three generations?

36%
CHANCE OF YESNew public record by 2029-12-31
Issued 5 November 2026 · open forecast

Subjective estimate, not an empirical base rate or a singularity probability.

Why we think this may happen

  • MASS describes training updated weights and repeating the shared-model loop; it is relevant to the specified object of improvement, unlike code-only scaffold modification. Its public report is evidence of a programme, not independent validation.
  • AIDE² supplies a separate example of repeated optimisation and held-out transfer under a cost budget. It makes multi-step research credible while leaving the checkpoint criterion unresolved.
  • By the deadline, more than three years remain for at least one team and one unaffiliated evaluator to pursue a bounded task distribution. The question does not require frontier-scale models or broad general intelligence, which prevents treating it as a forecast of singularity.

Why we might be wrong

  • The estimate could be too low: a deliberately weak initial checkpoint on a bounded distribution could permit three five-point gains without any general recursive intelligence breakthrough; no minimum initial competence or task breadth is specified.
  • The estimate could be too high: every successive gain must clear the same absolute threshold, so plateauing after one or two generations fails even when the overall result is useful.
  • The estimate could be too high: research incentives may favour new benchmark records over preregistration and unaffiliated reproduction; a technically real but privately validated result still resolves NO.
  • MASS self-evaluation and harness transfer are not the required external replication. Their author claims could overstate robust transfer, and neither is treated as an already qualifying case.
Exact outcome, timeframe & update signals +
What counts as YES
A qualifying public record must first be published from 6 November 2026 through 2029-12-31. Previously published cases inform this forecast but do not count as outcomes. An unaffiliated evaluator reproduces three successive model-improvement generations. Before generation one, the team registers an isolated held-out task distribution, fixed per-generation compute budget and regression limits. Every generation gains at least five percentage points in held-out task success within that budget and breaches no registered regression limit. Public code, lineage, settings and evaluator results are required by the deadline. Model improvement means new model weights or checkpoints, including training methods yielding new checkpoints. Harness-only changes do not qualify.
Resolution source & edge cases
Public preregistration, lineage and independent evaluation. Any missing gate disqualifies a result. No fully qualifying public three-generation result by the deadline resolves NO. Only records first published within the stated prospective observation window count.
Observation window
6 November 2026 through 2029-12-31 at 23:59 UTC. Criteria version 1.0. Previously published cases do not count as new outcomes.
Evidence that would raise the probability
A prospective public preregistration is followed by an unaffiliated reproduction of the first two checkpoint generations, each gaining at least five points under unchanged per-generation compute and passing registered regressions; third-generation candidate and code are available. Apply only to genuinely new evidence, not reannouncement. Proposed likelihood-ratio multiplier: 2.5. This is an update rule for review, not an automatic score.
Evidence that would lower it
By 2028-12-31 no public effort has reproduced even two qualifying checkpoint generations, or a leading candidate loses its gains under the registered held-out test or violates budget/regression gates. Proposed likelihood-ratio multiplier: 0.45. This is an update rule for review, not an automatic score.
How we estimated this +
One contributing analyst’s starting point
Subjective outside-view prior fixed before inspecting current case evidence: 25% for a new, publicly documented, preregistered and independently reproduced three-generation model-improvement milestone within roughly three years. There is no defensible matched cohort or numerator/denominator, so this is not an empirical base rate.
Reference-class limitations
Candidate classes considered: iterative self-training/model adaptation; self-modifying agent-harness research; and independent replication of preregistered machine-learning claims. They differ in object improved, budget accounting and disclosure incentives. None supplies a countable matched class for this exact conjunction. The narrow model-checkpoint requirement excludes harness-only successes.
Combining perspectives
Equal-weight geometric mean of odds from two separately elicited research perspectives, with no extremizing. They share model-family and source dependencies; this is not an independent human ensemble or evidence of calibration.
Limits of confidence
Subjective probability, not an empirical base rate. No matched reference-class frequency was found. Whole-percentage presentation does not imply one-point precision. Analyst spread is disagreement, not a confidence interval.
Separately elicited views
34% / 38%. The spread reflects analyst disagreement, not a confidence interval. Shared model-family and source dependencies limit the ensemble.

Q04 / Autonomous workBY 2030-12-31

Can an organisation close a consequential production loop?

60%
CHANCE OF YESNew public record by 2030-12-31
Issued 5 November 2026 · open forecast

Subjective estimate, not an empirical base rate or a singularity probability.

Why we think this may happen

  • DARPA’s published results establish autonomous discovery and generated patches on substantial real-world software, including non-synthetic vulnerabilities. They support feasibility of the first two links; the competition does not itself meet the production criterion.
  • Google’s deployment documentation separately supports automated promotion and rollback mechanisms. Those are existing engineering ingredients rather than a speculative capability that must first be invented.
  • The target requires one bounded organisation and one qualifying substantive security patch, not general unattended operation across an enterprise. Prior human policy authorisation is compatible with no approval between discovery and deployment, provided the audited path confirms that distinction.
  • The roughly four-year horizon leaves time for capability, constrained deployment policy and independent assurance to converge. This is a forecast of a documented milestone, not a claim that removing approval is appropriate everywhere.

Why we might be wrong

  • The estimate could be too high: major vendor workflows retain human review, and a working prototype may never obtain permission for unattended production changes.
  • The estimate could be too high: organisations may operate such loops privately but withhold vulnerability details, audit records or failed-recovery evidence; absent a qualifying public record the answer remains NO.
  • The estimate could be too low: a small service with narrow blast radius, mature automated tests and pre-authorised rollback could meet the conjunction well before broad enterprise adoption.
  • Published discovery and patching benchmarks do not measure production safety. Technical evidence is being combined with conventional deployment tools as a forecast inference, not as an already demonstrated integrated system.
Exact outcome, timeframe & update signals +
What counts as YES
A qualifying public record must first be published from 6 November 2026 through 2030-12-31. Previously published cases inform this forecast but do not count as outcomes. A named organisation publicly documents vulnerability discovery, substantive code patching and production deployment without human approval between discovery and deployment, plus verified automated rollback capability. An independent audit must confirm the production setting and decision path. Configuration or dependency bumps alone do not qualify. This public question adds an audit requirement and is not identical to any earlier internal forecast.
Resolution source & edge cases
Public organisation records and an unaffiliated audit. All criteria and records must exist by the deadline; no qualifying record resolves NO. Only records first published within the stated prospective observation window count.
Observation window
6 November 2026 through 2030-12-31 at 23:59 UTC. Criteria version 1.0. Previously published cases do not count as new outcomes.
Evidence that would raise the probability
An unaffiliated audit publicly confirms a prospective bounded production service that automatically ships substantive non-dependency patches and demonstrates rollback, with vulnerability discovery already integrated but some qualifying evidence still incomplete. Proposed likelihood-ratio multiplier: 2.2. This is an update rule for review, not an automatic score.
Evidence that would lower it
By 2029-12-31 leading candidates still require an intervening human approval, or a well-audited serious autonomous-patching incident causes sustained withdrawal of unattended production permissions. Proposed likelihood-ratio multiplier: 0.4. This is an update rule for review, not an automatic score.
How we estimated this +
One contributing analyst’s starting point
Subjective outside-view prior fixed before case-specific research: 55% that at least one named organisation publishes a qualifying audited autonomous security-to-production loop in roughly four years. No matched empirical adoption cohort combines discovery, substantive patching, no intervening approval, verified rollback and public independent audit; no historical success frequency is asserted.
Reference-class limitations
Candidate analogues are autonomous vulnerability-discovery/patching systems, conventional automated delivery-and-rollback systems, and audited enterprise deployment adoption. Contest success rates are not production-adoption rates. Agent-created PRs, human-approved patches, dependency updates and sandbox demonstrations do not count as the target event.
Combining perspectives
Equal-weight geometric mean of odds from two separately elicited research perspectives, with no extremizing. They share model-family and source dependencies; this is not an independent human ensemble or evidence of calibration.
Limits of confidence
Subjective probability, not an empirical base rate. No matched reference-class frequency was found. Whole-percentage presentation does not imply one-point precision. Analyst spread is disagreement, not a confidence interval.
Separately elicited views
63% / 57%. The spread reflects analyst disagreement, not a confidence interval. Shared model-family and source dependencies limit the ensemble.

FORECASTING, NOT DECORATION

Before publishing a number: define the reference class, weigh evidence for and against, compare separately elicited assessments, record the probability and name its update triggers. At resolution: score it and retain the lesson. A Brier score measures accuracy on those questions; it does not validate a singularity-distance scale.

Four forecasts were registered on 5 November 2026 with fixed prospective criteria, probabilities and opposing cases. No resolved outcomes are available for this series, so calibration is not yet measured. Earlier internal forecasts remain separate. This is a reviewed snapshot, not automatic monitoring.

03 / KEEP THE RECEIPTS

WHAT CHANGED / AND WHY

Revision is
part of the work.

2026-11-05

Initial public evidence review

Four selected source events were reviewed, including the follow-up that limits a present-day reading of the earlier productivity study. Four milestone questions were drafted. No numerical forecasts were issued, no historical probabilities were recalibrated, and no singularity-distance score was created.

INITIAL FORECASTS ISSUED: 0 · PROBABILITY REVISIONS: 0
2026-11-05

Access, work and mathematical evidence added; first forecasts registered

Added ChatGPT, Opus 4.5 and distinct proof/discovery/verification milestones, including a public proof correction. Before issuing probabilities, draft questions were clarified to count only new public records from 6 November 2026. Historical physical-design examples therefore inform priors without resolving new forecasts. Four initial probabilities are now recorded with opposing cases, deadlines and update triggers. No percentage distance to singularity is inferred.

INITIAL FORECASTS ISSUED: 4 · PROBABILITY REVISIONS: 0
2026-11-06

AI-accelerated research and a disputed proof added

Added METR's assessment of AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic, OpenAI's claimed Navier–Stokes proof and the independent challenge to its Lean formalization. All three predate the 6 November 2026 observation window and none meets a registered criterion, so all four probabilities are unchanged. The Navier–Stokes dispute shows that a passing formal proof can check a statement weaker than the claimed theorem. Whether the independent-research criteria should also require the formal statement to be independently matched to the claim is an open question for the 5 February 2027 review. Any change would be a superseding question, never an edit to an issued record.

INITIAL FORECASTS ISSUED: 0 · PROBABILITY REVISIONS: 0
2026-11-07

Autonomous Linux exploit and patch pipeline added

Added OpenAI's report of 948 unique Linux privilege-escalation exploits found, validated and patched by an automated pipeline. It predates the 6 November 2026 observation window and includes no production deployment, rollback or audit, so no question resolves. Production-loop is unchanged at 60%. The report strengthens the discovery and patching links the estimate already credited from DARPA's challenge and Aardvark, and its argument that automated patching is now necessary adds pressure in favour of the loop. Against it, human review still sits before every report, generated patches needed iteration, and an early run scored exploits that reached root through the wrong vulnerability. Neither registered update trigger has occurred. The other three questions are unaffected: a stronger model on an unchanged harness is not a registered improvement generation, and the withheld exploitation techniques cannot be independently checked.

INITIAL FORECASTS ISSUED: 0 · PROBABILITY REVISIONS: 0

HOW THE POSITION CHANGES

  1. Record the event. Retain its date, source and research lineage.
  2. Test the criterion. Distinguish a new capability from another announcement of the same result.
  3. Revise a registered forecast. Explain the evidence, retain the prior and consider both directions. No change is a valid conclusion.
  4. Show the revision. Keep the registered initial probability and every subsequent revision visible. Failed expectations and retractions can move the outlook back; calendar time never moves backward.

Demonstrated milestones change our picture of the future. They are not a percentage of the journey to singularity.
